import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 862

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/862](https://www.erdosproblems.com/862)
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. (1992),
  34-50.
- [SaTh15] Saxton, David and Thomason, Andrew, *Hypergraph containers*. Invent. Math. (2015),
  925-992.
-/

open Finset Filter

namespace Erdos862

/--
$A_1(N)$, the number of maximal Sidon subsets of $\{1, \dots, N\}$.
-/
noncomputable def numMaximalSidonSets (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  {A : Finset ℕ | A ⊆ Icc 1 N ∧ Set.IsMaximalSidonSetIn (A : Set ℕ) N}.ncard

/--
Let $A_1(N)$ be the number of maximal Sidon subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Is it true that
$$A_1(N) < 2^{o(N^{1/2})}?$$

A problem of Cameron and Erdős. This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and
Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least
$2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each
maximal Sidon set contains at most $2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos862.lean"]
theorem erdos_862.parts.i : answer(False) ↔
    (fun N : ℕ => Real.logb 2 (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $A_1(N)$ be the number of maximal Sidon subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Is it true that
$$A_1(N) > 2^{N^c}$$
for some constant $c>0$?

A problem of Cameron and Erdős. This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and
Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least
$2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each
maximal Sidon set contains at most $2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos862.lean"]
theorem erdos_862.parts.ii : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ ((N : ℝ) ^ c) < (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that
the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least $2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each
Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each maximal Sidon set contains at most
$2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_862.variants.lower_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ (((0.16 : ℝ) - ε) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) ≤ (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos862

reformulations.difference: The Lean RHS states log₂ A₁(N) = o(√N), rather than the exponential upper bound. Erdős's original equation (15) asks for A₁(N) < 2^(ε√N) for every ε > 0, asymptotically.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The count is finite and at least 1 for every N, so its logarithm is nonnegative. Little-o gives log₂ A₁(N) ≤ (ε/2)√N eventually, hence A₁(N) < 2^(ε√N) once N > 0. Conversely, taking logarithms of the eventual exponential inequalities gives all the bounds required for little-o. The exact equivalence with the strict ε-form was proved as Review862.part_i_reformulation in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the problem's sorry theorems.

reformulations.difference: The asymptotic lower bound A₁(N) ≥ 2^((0.16 + o(1))√N) is expressed using an arbitrary positive ε and the eventual bound 2^((0.16 − ε)√N) ≤ A₁(N).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A vanishing error term is eventually greater than −ε, which implies the ε-form. Conversely, for N > 0 set e(N) = min(log₂ A₁(N)/√N − 0.16, 0). The ε-bounds imply e(N) → 0, and its definition gives 2^((0.16 + e(N))√N) ≤ A₁(N). The equivalence with an existential o(1) error term was proved as Review862.lower_bound_reformulation_littleo in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Erdős, P., Some of my forgotten problems in number theory, Hardy–Ramanujan Journal 15 (1992), 34–50, especially §2, p. 39, equations (15)–(16): https://hrj.episciences.org/125/pdf
Saxton, D. and Thomason, A., Hypergraph containers, arXiv:1204.6595v3, §1.6, Theorem 1.11 and the preceding Sidon-set size bound; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1204.6595

Cited external Lean proof, especially MaximalSidonSubset, A1, cor_answers_1_unconditional and cor_answers_2_unconditional: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plby/lean-proofs/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos862.lean
review.notes: All four declarations were checked. Scratch proofs establish that the counted family is finite, that its count is positive for every N, and that single-element nonextendibility is equivalent to inclusion-maximality. Computation for N = 0,…,10 gives counts 1,1,1,3,3,6,14,20,24,36,64. The scratch file compiles without errors or warnings, and the verification lemmas use only standard axioms. Saxton–Thomason's counting bound, together with the stated Erdős–Turán size bound, yields the 0.16 lower bound and supports both recorded answers. The linked Lean proof's unconditional corollaries imply the file's answers after translating [0,N−1] to [1,N], rescaling the logarithm, and reducing c to obtain strict inequality. No sorry or custom axioms occur in the inspected external file; its project was not rebuilt because PrimeNumberTheoremAnd is unavailable in the sandbox. The live erdosproblems.com/862 page returned Cloudflare 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so the mathematical comparison used the cited primary papers directly rather than the page's latest remarks.
